preamble: Flowproof is a small language for orchestrating coding agents. Write one Flowproof workflow that meets every requirement below. Reply with only the workflow inside a single fenced code block.

specs.name: best_of_three
specs.text: Input `issue` (text). Role `author` edits; role `reviewer` only answers. Make three isolated attempts in which the author fixes the issue. Grade every attempt with `python -m pytest -q`, freezing `tests/**`. Choose by tests, then let the reviewer judge pairwise; if still tied, abstain. Fail with a message if the chosen attempt did not pass. Give the chosen attempt. Budget: at most 40 credits and 10 calls.

specs.name: repair_loop
specs.text: Input `task` (text). One role `author` that edits. The author attempts the task once; grade it with `python -m unittest`, freezing `tests/**`. If it did not pass, repeat at most three times: have the author fix the code, showing it the failing test output, then grade again. Finally require a pass and give the last grade. Budget: 4 calls.

specs.name: review_fanout
specs.text: Input `summary` (text). Roles `scout` and `reviewer` only answer. The scout lists the files likely affected by the summary (a list). The reviewer reviews at most four of them, one at a time. The scout then summarises the reviews. Give the summary. Budget: 6 calls.

specs.name: plan_then_edit
specs.text: Input `goal` (text). Role `planner` only answers; role `coder` edits. The planner writes a plan for the goal, the coder implements the plan, and then the workflow runs `python -m pytest -q` as a command. Give the command's result. Budget: 2 calls and 10 credits.

specs.name: vote_exact
specs.text: Input `issue` (text). Role `author` edits. Make five isolated attempts at the issue. Grade them all with `npm test`, freezing both `test/**` and `package.json`. Choose by tests, then by behaviour, then by exact patch votes, and fall back to the first candidate. Give it. Budget: 5 calls.

specs.name: guarded_question
specs.text: Inputs `question` (text) and `strict` (bool, default true). Role `analyst` only answers. Ask the analyst whether the repository already implements what the question describes, as a yes/no answer. If strict and the answer is no, fail with the message 'not implemented'. Give the answer. Budget: 1 call.

specs.name: count_and_fanout
specs.text: Input `topic` (text). Role `analyst` only answers. Ask the analyst how many independent sub-questions the topic has, as a number. Then ask three analysts at once, without isolating them because they only answer, for an answer to the topic each, and give all three answers. Budget: 4 calls.

specs.name: judge_answers
specs.text: Input `prompt` (text). Roles `writer` and `judge` only answer. Four writers each draft a response at once (no isolation needed). The judge picks the best one by pairwise comparison; if that is a tie, take the first. Give the choice. Budget: at most 20 calls.

specs.name: iterative_review
specs.text: Input `task` (text). Role `author` edits; role `critic` only answers. The author makes a change for the task. Then, at most twice, until the critic approves: ask the critic whether the latest change is acceptable (yes/no), and if it is not, have the author revise it. Give the final change. Budget: 5 calls.

specs.name: lint_gate
specs.text: Input `ticket` (text). Role `author` edits. The author makes the change; write a note saying 'edit done'; run `make lint` as a command and require that it succeeded, with the message 'lint failed'; then give the change. Budget: 1 call and 5 credits.

specs.name: isolated_shell
specs.text: Input `target` (text). Role `builder` can edit and run shell commands. Make two isolated attempts by the builder to build the target. Grade each with `cargo test`, freezing `tests/**`. Choose by tests and otherwise abstain. Give the choice. Budget: 2 calls.

specs.name: triage_and_fix
specs.text: Input `pr` (text). Role `triager` only answers; role `fixer` edits. The triager lists the problems in the pull request (a list). For each problem, at most three, the fixer fixes it in the shared workspace (no forks). Then run `pytest` as a command and give its result. Budget: 4 calls.
